feed.title: PHP2Shell — timeline (EN)
feed.subtitle: Live timeline of PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618/109619), a critical PHP core RCE (CVSS 9.2). Fixed in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35. Every fact sourced.

entry.title: SecurityWeek: vendor response roundup; Sophos took its own MyUTM portal offline
entry.summary: According to SecurityWeek, Sophos found that its MyUTM portal (a legacy licensing service for the end-of-life SG UTM) was running a vulnerable PHP version and took it offline on 21 Oct until it is updated. The same roundup reports that Fortinet confirmed about two dozen products are not impacted and that SolarWinds applied compensating controls to Pingdom.
entry.content:
According to SecurityWeek, Sophos found that its MyUTM portal (a legacy licensing service for the end-of-life SG UTM) was running a vulnerable PHP version and took it offline on 21 Oct until it is updated. The same roundup reports that Fortinet confirmed about two dozen products are not impacted and that SolarWinds applied compensating controls to Pingdom.

Source: SecurityWeek (Eduard Kovacs) · reported · minor

entry.title: Scale of attempts: Cloudflare reports millions, Censys about 1.57M unpatched hosts; watchTowr says circulating PoCs don't achieve RCE
entry.summary: SecurityWeek (22 Oct) rounds up telemetry: Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince said thousands of attempts in the 10 hours before the announcement, tens of thousands in the 45 minutes after, hundreds of thousands within 2 hours and "millions now". Censys: of 2.58M hosts seen on 21 Oct, about 1.58M exposed a PHP version and about 1.57M were unpatched. watchTowr: broad attempts, but circulating exploits don't work, only test timing differences, or crash the target. Figures are company statements; no confirmed compromises.

entry.title: heise: precautionary takedowns in Germany too (Charité, parts of berlin.de, Berlin police online station); most distros ship packages; no successful attacks reported
entry.summary: heise (Dirk Knop), citing dpa: Charité took its websites fully offline, parts of the berlin.de portal were switched off, the Berlin police online station was unreachable and Freie Universität Berlin restricted IT services; authority and police sites in Bavaria and Lower Saxony, among others, were also down, and the first sites in the north are back (NDR). Per Reuters, government sites went offline in Denmark, Finland, France and the Netherlands. Updated packages: Debian, Fedora, Gentoo, Ubuntu, Red Hat, Slackware, SUSE. heise: many exploit attempts, but at the time of writing no reports of successful attacks. The shutdowns are described as precautionary.

entry.summary: Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince posted that in the 10 hours before PHP2Shell was publicly announced the Cloudflare network saw thousands of exploitation attempts, tens of thousands in the 45 minutes after, hundreds of thousands within 2 hours and “millions now”. It is a second sensor network, independent of AWS, that saw attempts before the patch release (AWS MadPot: from about 02:00 UTC on 21 Oct), though after the 20 Oct leak. The figures count attempts, not successful break-ins; Cloudflare published no breakdown.

entry.title: Regression in 8.4.27/8.5.12: SimpleXML double free during GC (GH-24488)
entry.summary: php-src report (label “Status: Verified”): since the GH-24050 fix, the garbage collector can free a SimpleXMLElement properties table twice (“zend_mm_heap corrupted”); 8.4.26 is not affected. A PHP maintainer agrees with the diagnosis; a one-line fix (PR #24494) awaits merging. This is a stability bug with no CVE and no demonstrated remote exploitation; it does not show that the CVE-2026-109618/109619 fixes fail. It may be behind the “second double free in 8.5.12” rumour — unconfirmed.

entry.title: Fastly: “evidence of attacks before disclosure” and a warning that the problem sits in the engine's design
entry.summary: Kelly Shortridge (Fastly CPO) writes of “evidence of active attacks in-the-wild pre-disclosure”, without publishing data. The emergency request-abort mechanism (zend_bailout/longjmp) appears in many places in the code, so the patches close only the paths found; Fastly expects new variants “this week and next”. Mitigating detail: known PoCs on x86_64 need knowledge of the specific binary and memory layout of the server. Fastly says it will publish its own telemetry.

entry.title: PHP Foundation: the OOM problem was known since the 2024 audit, the fix stalled for months
entry.summary: The foundation describes the backstory. Its developer found the first signs of the out-of-memory (OOM) problem in 2024 while fixing an issue from the Quarkslab audit (funded by Germany's Sovereign Tech Agency via OSTIF). An exploit was only theorised, and the consensus-driven security team could not choose between several flawed fixes, so work stalled and restarted repeatedly. The foundation calls this a “structural failure”. Calif began its audit on 30 July 2026; on 11 August Ryan A at Calif and OpenAI independently reported the same root cause, Wiz followed on 24 August and OpenAI added vectors on 18 September. Trail of Bits is now auditing as well. Since 1 July the team has published 15 CVEs and worked through more than 100 invalid reports.

entry.title: Calif publishes the full technical write-up and its own timeline
entry.summary: Ryan Austin (Calif): first RCE paths found on 1 Aug, a hash of one finding posted on X on 5 Aug, first report to PHP on 11 Aug, PoC on 14 Aug, confirmed by PHP on 15 Aug, second bug reported on 21 Aug. Root cause (in line with the advisories): an out-of-memory error interrupts request processing halfway and internal state survives pointing into freed memory. Calif traces the story back to Stefan Esser’s 2004 bug, report #78876 from 2020 and the 2024 OSTIF/Quarkslab audit.

entry.title: PHP security team member: the fix turns memory_limit into a soft limit
entry.summary: Alexandre Daubois explains the fix at diff level: the allocator no longer jumps out (bailout) in the middle of an allocation; exceeding memory_limit records a deferred error and the request stops at a safe point. A new hard limit, memory_hard_limit_percent (default 200% of memory_limit below 1G), ends the process. The fix touches 390 files. Timeline: advisory opened 27 Aug 2026, fix PR opened 25 Sep 2026. He stresses that the most repeated advice (session.upload_progress.enabled = Off) only applies to CVE-2026-109619.

entry.title: CrowdStrike: remote code execution verified in the lab on Apache mod_php
entry.summary: CrowdStrike (Amit Serper) says it verified the full chain: a single anonymous POST request made an Apache mod_php worker launch a shell and run a command, with no authentication and no vulnerable application code. The exploit has not been published. According to CrowdStrike, PHP’s shipped defaults (post_max_size 8M, memory_limit 128M) cannot be driven into the bug along the path it demonstrated; exposed are configurations with memory_limit below roughly 4 × post_max_size. Trace for defenders: a memory-exhaustion fatal error “in Unknown on line 0” in the web server log.

entry.title: AWS: PHP2Shell exploitation attempt seen in MadPot honeypots on 17 Oct, four days before disclosure
entry.summary: Amazon Threat Intelligence (post by CJ Moses, 21 Oct) says MadPot telemetry recorded an exploitation attempt on 17 Oct from a commercial anonymisation network, while the embargo was in force; how the actor obtained the information is unknown. On 21 Oct from about 02:00 to 08:00 UTC further attempts came from varied infrastructure (likely multiple actors); after 14:00 UTC AWS describes broad exploitation, but it is unclear whether any attempt would have succeeded on real systems. Advice: start investigations from at least 17 Oct.
